year.label: 2020 BMW M2 CS Racing customer-racing launch

identity.real_world_identity_notes: BMW M2 CS Racing is BMW M Motorsport's close-to-production customer-racing car based on the M2 CS. BMW documentation identifies the 2020 car with a seven-speed dual-clutch gearbox using motorsport software and steering-wheel paddle shifting. The exact BMW 09/2020 cockpit photograph shows molded left/right grips with a central control face, establishing a gt-formula rim, plus paddle shifters and a separate display. The RFactor2 observation's seven-speed count agrees with the real car; its automatic-blip value remains simulator evidence only.

BMW M Motorsport's model page and launch release identify the BMW M2 CS Racing as a customer-racing vehicle and place its launch in 2020. BMW's technical customer manual identifies the 2020 car and documents the seven-speed double-clutch transmission, paddle-shift controls, and sequential mode. The exact-car BMW PressClub photo confirms the GT-formula wheel topology. The repository contains no curated BMW M2 CS Racing record, so this case proposes a new real-car record.

claims.basis: BMW M Motorsport's model page and launch release identify the BMW M2 CS Racing as a customer-racing vehicle and place its launch in 2020. BMW's technical customer manual identifies the 2020 car and documents the seven-speed double-clutch transmission, paddle-shift controls, and sequential mode. The exact-car BMW PressClub photo confirms the GT-formula wheel topology. The repository contains no curated BMW M2 CS Racing record, so this case proposes a new real-car record.

The exact BMW M2 CS Racing photograph visibly shows molded left/right grips with a central control face between them, meeting the repository definition of gt-formula. This is a direct rim observation, not a class-based inference. BMW specifies a seven-speed dual-clutch transmission, and the technical manual lists gears 1 through 7 and reverse. This agrees with the staged RFactor2 seven-speed observation. BMW explicitly describes the transmission as seven-speed dual-clutch/double-clutch with motorsport software. BMW documents a removable BMW Motorsport steering wheel with shift paddles; the technical manual specifies paddle-shift up and down controls, also visible in the exact photo. The technical manual describes D/S as the change between Drive Mode and sequential shift Mode and documents manual + and - selector positions.
